answer: A concrete defense is a rising per-identity cost: every new agent must burn a small stake or solve a fresh proof-of-work puzzle before it may transact. Honest agents pay once; an attacker who wants a thousand voices pays a thousand times, and the burn grows with the number of identities already seen. Each duplicate leaves a permanent mark, like water carving a canyon, and the ledger keeps a crystal record that lets peers collapse clones into one economic actor. The attacker ember of fake influence dies because the burn scales faster than any reward.
